questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have previously lived here with my family, and I was interested in getting better at French as well as I was interested in EU-law.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit different from UCPH, since you don't need to sign up for classes before arrvial because you spend the first two weeks trying out the classes, that you might like. I feel like a lot of information was accessible on the website of ULB but the website was a bit difficult to navigate in the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received e-mails before arriving and had information sessions when we arrived. I feel like the level of information was sufficient, but you need to have faith in the fact that everything will work out and don't stress it too much.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was quite easy for me since I got a spot in the dorm at The Danish Church in Bruxelles. There are not that many rooms so I would advise people to sign up as soon as possible. The area, Ixelles, is very nice, the dorm is old, but it has been very cosy living with other young Danes.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start looking early and think about the area!! Ixelles and Saint-Gilles are quite nice neighbourhoods.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They were flexible and offered help regarding changing the OLA as well as getting registered for the right courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once you has decided on the classes to follow, you had to change the OLA and get it signed from the responsible person. This was the wat of registerering for coureses, and even though it took some time it went quite smooth.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The responsible person from the law faculty was available if you needed help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very succesfull. It seemed like there were no limitations regarding the number of students for each class, so there were not stress and I got all of the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Take it easy, try out the different courses, talk to the other students, Erasmus as well as locals regarding their experiences with the different courses. Don't worry too much about registration, there is room for everyone. 

I chose my courses based on interests, but you have to "make" your own schedule, so have a look at the platform from ULB, Timeedit, and make sure that the courses fit in your schedule and daily life.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one bachelor course and four master courses. The level were quite okay to follow. I took two courses in french, which was possible even though I am only in the beginning of B2. I did not praticipate in any of the travaux practique since it were not mandatory to exchange students in my courses. This made the work load quite easy compared to Copenhagen. The bachelor course I took were very explanatory and not so elaborative, so I am glad I didn't only sign up for bachelor courses since the level of these were quite low.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very much lecture-style with little participation. I took a lot of courses from the LLM in European Law, where more participation was expected. Furthermore, there are not any books, only PowerPoints and certain documents issued by the EU-insitutions were part of the curriculum in my experience. Therefore, it usually made more sense to study after a session than before. All exams are handwritten and mostly closed book, but with the treaties or other legislation/documents issued by institutions. I was more worried about this than needed, but it is nice to know and to be prepared for.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Droit de l'Union européenne DROIC-3003 10 ECTS, bachelor level
Law of aremd conflicts DROIC-5149 - 5 ECTS
EU competition law, DROIC687 - 5 ECTS
Protection juridictionelle dans l'Union européenne, DROIO500 - 5 ECTS
Internal market with a focus on Free Movement of Goods - DROIO627 - 5 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think that all of the courses I took were quite interesting. The most challenging, but also interesting was Protection jurdictionelle since this gave me a new perspective on EU and the legal certainty.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not anything really, transportation is 18 euros for a card with unlimited transport for a year, and you can get access to the gym at ULB for 36 euros for a semester. Groceries are quite the same as in Copenhagen, so is eating in restaurant. Beers and coffees are quite cheap. So is fries.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: See the section above

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got the ULB sports card and both used the gym as well as went to different sport classes. These were very nice a a great option to do with friends.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus-organisation arranged a lot of different things, which I went to a few of. I did however spend a lot of timw with my housemates, and did not go as much as other people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do the sports, go to Plux on THursdays and just have a great time. Enjoy the vivid life in Bruxelles, and to the cafés since there are so many nice ones.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit cities in Bruxelles. Bruxelles is very centrally placed in Europe, and people often go to Paris, Amsterdam etc. I think that Ghent, Brugge, Antwerpen etc all are quite nice and cosy cities so try to visit if you have time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. The Belgian culture is a lot like the danish one, exempt for the fact that people go out to eat/drink a lot more. I would recommend to implemt this habit!!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you have more than one cours with some students then try talking to them, get into the Whatsapp groups and such. People are friendly, but in my experience you usually need to be the one to approach. Thias can be difficult, but once you have done it is very nice and helpful to have someone to asks regarding exam, french things you don't understand and such.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find anything that challenging. Maybe the language sometimes, but ULB also offers classes which was helpful

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The vivid life and people using the city so much.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the city, don't underestimate it. Try the fries with a polycrouc, it is very delicious, find a great crowd and don't be afraid to intiate things. Everyone is there to make friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so, generally ULB was quite heplful. Trust the proces, even though it is different fromm UCPH.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new lovely people, getting a new perspective on EU-law and improving my french.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was actually a lot less challenging than expected. I missed people from back home, but had visits, which was great. Generally it has been really lovely!!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
